Oakmoss, for example, has been used in perfumes for more than one hundred years. When it was discovered that oakmoss is an allergen and its use was restricted, perfumers were in trouble. The French company Mane responded by creating a substitute from other materials. Hydroxycitronellal, an ingredient often used to add a floral note to perfumes, was also restricted. Andy Tauer, a Swiss perfumer, blended different combinations of chemicals together to make up for this restriction.
